facts.claim: Geofabrik hosts regional .osm.pbf extracts at download.geofabrik.de
Geofabrik footer states data licence ODbL 1.0, credits OpenStreetMap Contributors, processed by Geofabrik GmbH
Small country extracts (Luxembourg, Liechtenstein, Monaco) are listed on the top-level page
Smallest extract on the top-level page is Antarctica at 31.6 MB; continent extracts range 31.6 MB to 32.9 GB
OSM data is licensed under ODbL; full legal code linked points to version 1.0
ODbL requires attribution and share-alike of altered or built-upon data (no Derived Database / Produced Work distinction on the page)
PBF format: BlobHeader/Blob container, zlib-compressed blocks, PrimitiveBlock with DenseNodes delta encoding, granularity and offsets
PBF format spec is a free-to-implement standard with a version number
osmpbf Rust crate provides parallel decoding (ElementReader::par_map_reduce) and is on crates.io/docs.rs
pyosmium is BSD-2-Clause; libosmium is BSL; osmium-tool is GPL-3.0-or-later
The DIMACS road routing task is a public benchmark task (seed band text)
A reference pipeline exists with a measured speedup over the baseline

spike_plan.kill_if: Decode speedup is under 1.5x on 8 cores (I/O or parse bound), or the checksum or distances vary between runs.
spike_plan.pass_if: Parallel decode gives at least 2x median speedup on 8 cores, and canonical checksum plus query distances are identical across all runs and variants.
steps: In a throwaway container with network, download one small Geofabrik country extract (Luxembourg or Liechtenstein) and record its size and sha256.
Write a minimal Rust baseline with the osmpbf crate: single-thread decode of road ways and nodes, then a simple adjacency graph.
Add a parallel variant with ElementReader::par_map_reduce and measure median wall-clock over 5 runs on 8 cores.
Define a layout-independent canonical graph checksum (sorted edge list with integer costs) and confirm it matches across baseline and parallel variants.
Run a 20-query point-to-point batch and check that integer distances are identical across runs.
Repeat the run in a second process to confirm determinism of checksum and distances.

v1.summary: The seed is real: Geofabrik extracts and the OSM PBF spec are public and the data is ODbL 1.0, but no upstream code, reference or measured speedup exists, so the pipeline and its reference must be built from scratch. The gate as written conflicts with the layout lever: an exact graph checksum would reject a better layout unless it is defined over a canonical, layout-independent form, and that must be fixed before the spike.
